xhs.opening_hook: Your top SKU might be wearing a label that drops conversion 20-40%. Amazon won't tell you.
thread: Your top Amazon SKU might be wearing a silent label that drops conversion 20-40%. The platform won't notify you. Most sellers find out 3-4 weeks late, after they've already burned ad spend at half the conversion rate. 🧵

It's called Frequently Returned. Amazon attaches it to the product detail page itself when a SKU's return rate exceeds the category baseline. Every shopper sees it before clicking buy. Many close the tab.

Trigger conditions are mechanical: return rate above category avg, returns clustering around "not as described," or post-promo spikes pushing the rate over the line. Spring promos and Prime Day are the two big landmines.

Once flagged, removal takes weeks of below-average returns. Prime Day 2026 is ~5 weeks out. If a SKU is borderline, you don't have time to fix it AND prove the fix worked before the event amplifies the problem.

What I'd do this week:
1. Pull the FBA returns report
2. Mark every SKU above category avg
3. Fix the detail page (real photos, sizing, materials)
4. For unfixable SKUs: pause ads or remove before Prime Day.

Operator move: stop spending behind broken SKUs *before* the platform decides for you. The badge isn't a punishment, it's lagging signal you've been ignoring.

#Amazon
